description:
Episode 78 of a daily journey through the universe. 🚀
Starship: SpaceX's giant rocket stands about 124 meters tall, the biggest and most powerful ever flown. Its booster is designed to be caught by the launch tower's 'chopsticks', and a version of Starship is planned as NASA's Moon lander.

segments.text: The Saturn five, which carried astronauts to the Moon, was a giant. But a new rocket is even bigger.
segments.headline: Saturn V

segments.text: Starship, built by SpaceX, is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever flown. About one hundred twenty-four meters tall.
It has two parts: a giant booster called Super Heavy, and the Starship spacecraft on top.
segments.headline: Two stages

segments.text: The big idea is to reuse everything, like an airplane, instead of throwing rockets away.
segments.headline: Reuse everything

segments.text: In October twenty twenty-four, the booster flew back to its launch tower, and giant mechanical arms, nicknamed chopsticks, caught it in midair.
segments.headline: Caught by chopsticks

segments.text: It has flown more than a dozen test flights, with explosions, fixes and big successes along the way.
NASA plans to use a version of Starship as a lander to put astronauts back on the Moon.
segments.headline: A Moon lander

segments.text: And SpaceX hopes one day to send it to Mars.
segments.headline: Next: Mars?

segments.text: Tomorrow, where Starship and astronauts are headed: the Moon's south pole. Next stop: the lunar south pole. Follow, so you don't miss episode seventy-nine.
